title: Search the literature
when: finding out, before any paid proving, whether a paper already proves, refutes or restricts a statement (the intake step of a run does this)
looking for the source and the known cases of a named conjecture
whenNot: proving anything: a hit is text from a third party and gives a lead, which only a Lean proof settles
a statement you cannot send to third parties: the run's --private option sends nothing outside
a quote you have not checked against the text of the hit

query.description: Words to search for, such as the keywords of the statement

limit.description: At most this many hits from each backend. 5 when not given

backends.description: Ask only these backends; absent: every one the host profile enables

text.description: The text the backend gave, cleaned and bounded: the only text a quote may come from

thirdParty.sends: search words taken from the statement, to OpenAlex, arXiv, Semantic Scholar and zbMATH

examples.title: a named conjecture

hits.title: A title
hits.text: The abstract as the site gives it.

examples.note: The hit is made up for this page; the real ones are the sites'.

implementations.description: The backends the host profile enables, each at its address with the hosts it may reach (https only, no redirect, an answer size limit, one request at a time with a pause). The requests and answers of OpenAlex, arXiv, Semantic Scholar and zbMATH are written from their documentation as remembered. Not run against any site: they are not reachable from the development environment.

environment.sites: api.openalex.org, export.arxiv.org, api.semanticscholar.org, api.zbmath.org, or the addresses OPENALEX_URL, ARXIV_URL, SEMANTIC_SCHOLAR_URL, ZBMATH_URL give (the host profile's allowedHosts must name the host); the bench checkout at BENCH_CHECKOUT
